page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-32GB is a virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 7542 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile with notable tradeoffs. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10% according to stress-ng testing, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores reach average levels, placing in the middle 50%. Memory performance is mixed; while read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks is average, large-block write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, static web serving throughput is weak, though database operations and Redis SET operations maintain average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and AMD EPYC hardware profile offer a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, multi-threaded background processing, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It is less optimal for high-throughput web serving or memory-write-intensive tasks due to the identified performance bottlenecks.
